rv.q: Towards the end the play, Mamet does find something to say... But we don't need this play to prove Mamet ...
It feels like a first draft, its silly and unsatisfactory second half needs rewriting.

cn.t: Mamet's satire of a Weinstein-like producer feels like an unfinished first draft that lurches between tones without landing on a clear point, ultimately proving listless and unsatisfying despite occasional sharp moments.
